It is categorized under text-generation pipelines, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the DeepSeek-V4-Pro model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized under text-generation and conversational AI pipelines.
It utilizes standard ML frameworks like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has secured significant funding, raising $88 million.
The funding round includes major investors such as Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama is rapidly gaining traction, serving 8.9 million developers in the open models space.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 performance is significantly boosted on Apple Silicon when run through Ollama 0.31.
The speed improvement is achieved via Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) leveraging the MLX framework.
Performance gains reach up to 90% faster, particularly when integrated with coding agents (Aider benchmark).

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance boost translates to higher quality model responses.
Improvements include faster response times and reduced memory consumption.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released as an open-source framework for personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run on user hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, facilitating the use of local LLMs.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance optimization.
This update specifically targets Apple Silicon hardware, enhancing local AI capabilities on Macs.
The feature is currently available in a preview release, indicating ongoing development.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a personal AI assistant designed to integrate with existing messaging applications.
It utilizes local AI coding agents, emphasizing on-device processing for privacy and control.
The core value proposition is bringing powerful AI capabilities directly to the user's personal device.

stories.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Quantum error correction is being advanced by using reinforcement learning.
The core mechanism involves using error information to dynamically adjust processor control algorithms.
This represents a significant step toward building stable and functional quantum processors.

stories.title: Ransomware negotiator hired to represent victims was working for the attackers
stories.author: Jon Brodkin
bullet_points: A ransomware negotiator was found to be working for the attackers he was hired to represent.
The individual was sentenced to six years in prison for betraying the victims.
The story highlights the severe risks and ethical breaches within the cybersecurity incident response industry.

stories.title: AUTOPILOT VQA: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Incident-Centric Dashcam Understanding
stories.author: Jugal Kalita
bullet_points: Introduces AUTOPILOT-VQA, a new benchmark specifically designed for incident-centric visual question answering in dashcam video.
Addresses a critical gap in current research: reliably evaluating Vision-Language Models (VLMs) for reasoning about safety-critical driving incidents.
Leverages advancements in VLMs and LLMs to push the boundaries of autonomous driving perception and safety assessment.

stories.title: The Illusion of Equivalency: Statistical Characterization of Quantization Effects in LLMs
stories.author: Carson K. Leung
bullet_points: Standard LLM evaluation (accuracy/perplexity) is insufficient for assessing quantization effects.
The paper introduces 'correctness agreement,' a new decision-level metric to measure behavioral changes post-quantization.
This research addresses a critical gap in deploying LLMs in resource-constrained environments by providing a more nuanced evaluation tool.

stories.title: Super Weights in LLMs and the Failure of Selective Training
stories.author: Akarsha Sehwag
bullet_points: Identifies 'Super Weights' in LLMs—parameters whose removal drastically degrades model performance.
Challenges the assumption that Super Weight-aware training is effective, showing isolation training causes severe accuracy drops.
Demonstrates that the concept of critical Super Weights is not universally applicable across all Large Language Models (LLMs).

stories.title: UniClawBench: A Universal Benchmark for Proactive Agents on Real-World Tasks
stories.author: Xihui Liu
bullet_points: Introduces UniClawBench, a new universal benchmark designed to evaluate proactive AI agents.
Addresses limitations in current benchmarks, which often use sandboxed environments and single-turn evaluations.
Focuses on assessing agents' capabilities in complex, real-world tasks rather than isolated functions.

stories.title: WebSwarm: Recursive Multi-Agent Orchestration for Deep-and-Wide Web Search
stories.author: Zhicheng Dou
bullet_points: WebSwarm introduces a recursive multi-agent orchestration framework to overcome limitations in current LLM-based web search.
Traditional single-agent approaches struggle with balancing deep, complex research trajectories against wide coverage.
The system addresses shortcomings in existing multi-agent systems, particularly concerning recursive depth and comprehensive search.

stories.title: UltraX: Refining Pre-Training Data at Scale with Adaptive Programmatic Editing
stories.author: Zhiyuan Liu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the diminishing returns of scaling laws as training data approaches limits.
It introduces 'UltraX,' a method for refining pre-training data at scale using adaptive programmatic editing.
UltraX aims to overcome limitations in existing refinement techniques (like rule-based approaches) regarding quality and efficiency.

stories.title: It Takes a MAESTRO To Prune Bad Experts
stories.author: Tanmoy Chakraborty
bullet_points: Addresses the deployment bottleneck in Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, where full expert banks remain in memory despite sparse activation.
Introduces MAESTRO, a new method designed to prune 'bad experts' in MoE models.
Overcomes limitations of existing pruning techniques by accounting for the interdependent nature of MoE routing, unlike methods designed for dense transformers.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 introduces significant performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now available via llama.cpp integration.
The update broadens model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA has introduced the Nemotron 3 Ultra model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search functionality within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the complexity and capability of AI agents managed via Ollama.

stories.title: China recovered its first reusable rocket and showed a new way to do it
stories.author: Stephen Clark
bullet_points: China has successfully recovered its first reusable rocket.
The recovery demonstrated a new methodology for achieving reusability.
The effort suggests an emulation of technologies pioneered by SpaceX.

stories.title: Firmware update bricks Hue Bridge Pro devices; Philips gives free replacements
stories.author: Scharon Harding
bullet_points: A firmware update has caused a critical failure (bricking) in Hue Bridge Pro devices.
Philips is providing free replacement units to affected customers.
Users impacted by the failure will need to reconfigure their entire smart lighting setup.

stories.title: OpenCoF: Learning to Reason Through Video Generation
stories.author: Hongsheng Li
bullet_points: Introduces OpenCoF, a new approach to enabling reasoning within video generation models.
Proposes Chain-of-Frame (CoF) reasoning, where logical consequences unfold across temporally connected video frames, distinct from traditional Chain-of-Thought (CoT).
Addresses a gap in current video generators, which lack specific supervision and design tailored for robust CoF reasoning.

stories.title: Ideas Have Genomes: Benchmarking Scientific Lineage Reasoning and Lineage-Grounded Idea Generation
stories.author: Xue Yang
bullet_points: Introduces IdeaGene-Bench (IG-Bench), a new benchmark for evaluating AI's ability to reason about scientific lineage.
Addresses the gap in current AI benchmarks regarding how scientific ideas evolve through inheritance and recombination, similar to biological genomes.
Focuses on testing 'lineage-grounded idea generation,' moving beyond simple idea creation to understanding intellectual history.

stories.title: Using AI-based Learning Assistants in Higher Education: A Large-Scale Descriptive Analysis
stories.author: Valerie Heckel
bullet_points: The study provides a large-scale, objective analysis of AI learning assistant usage (Syntea) in higher education.
It analyzes usage patterns across diverse student demographics, including gender, age, and study mode, using data from over 77,500 students.
The research addresses a gap in current literature by moving beyond small samples and self-reported survey data to examine actual usage behavior.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The model shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like measuring the moral foundation of authority.
The research cautions that high agreement (reliability) does not guarantee validity for complex, inferred theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometric accuracy, while real-world applications require biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has significant relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, ergonomics, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Score Accuracy Along the Forward Diffusion Does Not Certify Numerical Stability in Diffusion Sampling
stories.author: Yiwei Zhou
bullet_points: The paper challenges the assumption that low forward-marginal error in score matching guarantees numerical stability during diffusion sampling.
It demonstrates that a smooth score field with minimal forward error can still lead to a nonexplosive and stable reverse-time process.
This highlights a critical distinction between theoretical error bounds (forward marginals) and practical sampling behavior (reverse trajectory).

stories.title: SLORR: Simple and Efficient In-Training Low-Rank Regularization
stories.author: Shiwei Liu
bullet_points: SLORR introduces a new method for in-training low-rank regularization to improve neural network compressibility.
It addresses limitations of existing methods, such as reliance on SVDs of large matrices or architectural modifications.
The proposed technique is highlighted as being simple, stateless, and efficient.

stories.title: Dimensionality Reduction Meets Network Science: Sensemaking on UMAP's kNN Graph
stories.author: Dominik Moritz
bullet_points: The research focuses on leveraging the internal kNN graph constructed by UMAP, rather than just its final low-dimensional embedding.
This internal graph preserves the data manifold structure from the original high-dimensional space, avoiding projection distortion.
Applying standard graph algorithms to this graph enhances data sensemaking capabilities beyond typical UMAP usage.

stories.title: ARDY: Autoregressive Diffusion with Hybrid Representation for Interactive Human Motion Generation
stories.author: Davis Rempe
bullet_points: The research introduces ARDY, a new model for generating realistic 3D human motions.
It addresses the trade-off between high-quality, controllable offline motion generation and the real-time inference speed needed for interactive applications.
ARDY utilizes an autoregressive diffusion model with a hybrid representation to achieve both realism and interactivity.

stories.title: Pose-to-Biomechanics: Bridging 3D Human Pose Estimation and Biomechanical Attribute Prediction
stories.author: Kevin Desai
bullet_points: The research addresses a gap where 3D human pose estimation focuses on geometry, but real-world applications need biomechanical insights.
A new lightweight plug-in temporal transformer, 'BioModule,' is proposed to bridge the gap between pose estimation and biomechanical attribute prediction.
The technology has high relevance for fields like rehabilitation, sports science, and clinical movement analysis.

stories.title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
stories.author: Abhishek Gupta
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of transferring flexible, language-based reasoning from LLMs to continuous control policies.
Proposes a novel framework, 'Latent Memory Palace,' utilizing Autoregressive Variational Inference to structure information for control.
Aims to enable control policies to exhibit adaptive reasoning capabilities necessary for complex, deliberative actions.

stories.title: LTM: Large-scale Terrain Model for Wildfire-prone Landscapes
stories.author: Barath Raghavan
bullet_points: Addresses the critical need for accurate 3D terrain models in wildfire hazard assessment.
Proposes a multi-modal reconstruction framework to overcome limitations of expensive LiDAR and sparse image-based methods.
Focuses on improving terrain mapping accuracy over vast, wildfire-prone landscapes.

stories.title: Validity of LLMs as data annotators: AMALIA on authority
stories.author: Manuel Pita
bullet_points: Introduces AMALIA, a publicly funded 9B-parameter LLM specifically for European Portuguese.
The model shows competitive agreement with human coders on tasks like measuring the moral foundation of authority.
The research cautions that high agreement (reliability) does not guarantee validity when inferring theoretical constructs.

stories.title: Remember When It Matters: Proactive Memory Agent for Long-Horizon Agents
stories.author: Zhuokai Zhao
bullet_points: Addresses 'behavioral state decay' in long-horizon AI tasks where critical information gets lost in growing trajectories.
Proposes treating memory not as passive retrieval, but as an active intervention mechanism for agents.
Focuses on enabling agents to surface and utilize scattered, decision-relevant state information over long periods.

stories.title: Do You Need a Frontier Model as a Citation Verifier? Benchmarking Rubric LLMs for Deep-Research Source Attribution
stories.author: Kevin Paul
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical need to benchmark LLM judges used as reward models in reinforcement learning.
It specifically focuses on citation quality in deep-research systems, where LLMs must ground claims with cited sources.
The research investigates the calibration and potential bias of LLMs when performing structured rubric tasks for source attribution.

stories.title: DominoTree: Conditional Tree-Structured Drafting with Domino for Speculative Decoding
stories.author: Jyh-Shing Roger Jang
bullet_points: DominoTree introduces a new method for conditional tree-structured drafting to enhance speculative decoding in LLMs.
It addresses a limitation in existing methods (like DDTree) by incorporating a GRU-based causal correction, making draft token distributions path-dependent.
The research aims to accelerate LLM inference by improving the quality and structure of the tokens drafted before verification.

stories.title: The complexities of patient-centred conversational artificial intelligence
stories.author: Jonathan Amar
bullet_points: The study addresses a critical gap in health AI: the reliance on simulated patients for testing consumer-facing LLM chatbots.
Analysis of 2,053 real patient-chatbot conversations revealed high variability in user communication patterns and emotional expression.
Researchers developed a novel patient simulator capable of modeling clinical content, emotional state, conversational strategy, and communication style.

stories.title: Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius: Inside the Circular Financing of the GPU Boom
stories.author: adletbalzhanov
bullet_points: The article discusses the financial mechanisms driving the current GPU boom.
It focuses on the interplay between major players like Nvidia, CoreWeave, and Nebius.
The core theme is the 'circular financing' model supporting the rapid expansion of AI infrastructure.

stories.title: Personal Context vs. Shared Context: A Deep Dive Into How Humans and Organizations Should Feed Their AI Agents
stories.author: alexmercedcoder
bullet_points: The core issue in current AI agent failures is identified as context management.
The article explores the difference between personal context (individual knowledge) and shared context (organizational knowledge) for AI.
It provides guidance on how humans and organizations should structure and feed context to AI agents.
